_doc: Published by pipeline/standards_publish.mjs from pipeline/standards.json. Never edited by hand.

account_executive.label: Account Executive or SDR
account_executive.summary: Sales loops are live role-plays and small written or recorded pieces: a mock cold call or discovery call, often run twice to see how you take feedback, a cold email, a voicemail, a mock demo. Several employers publish theirs.

shows.label: A cold call
shows.means: Open, state the problem you solve, handle the first objection, ask for the meeting.
artifacts: A call script: opener, problem statement, objection responses
A recording of yourself running it
A 30-second voicemail pitch

shows.label: A discovery call
shows.means: Plan the questions that surface the buyer's problem and what it costs them. Ask them in order.
artifacts: A discovery call plan for one real company

shows.label: Taking feedback
shows.means: Run the call, critique it yourself, take one note and run it again better.
artifacts: Two recordings of the same call with what you changed

shows.label: An outbound sequence
shows.means: Pick a real prospect. Research them, write the cold email, and say why this account, this person and these words.
artifacts: A cold email to a researched prospect with a short rationale
A target account list with a sequence of short emails
The reply and meeting numbers, if you send them

shows.label: A qualified deal
shows.means: Take one real or realistic opportunity and say who decides, on what, by when and why.
artifacts: A deal sheet filled in for one opportunity

shows.label: A pitch that teaches the buyer something
shows.means: Reframe one buyer's problem with a fact they did not know. Tailor it to one person.
artifacts: A short insight pitch for a named role at a real company

shows.label: A product demo
shows.means: Demo a real product to a pretend buyer. Fit it to their problem, then send the follow-up email with next steps.
artifacts: A short recorded demo of a product you know
A follow-up proposal email

shows.label: A plan for your first months
shows.means: Say which accounts you would go after first, how you would build pipeline, and what you expect by when.
artifacts: A short pipeline and ramp plan for one real company's product

bizops.label: Business Operations Manager
bizops.summary: BizOps and Strategy & Operations loops centre on a take-home: a dataset, a day or two, then slides or a memo defended live. Startups add a paid work trial. Big tech companies do not publish their loops; the detail comes from two startups' own pages, DoorDash's careers blog and practitioners.

shows.label: A structured answer to a business problem
shows.means: Break a company's problem into parts. Size each and commit to a recommendation.
artifacts: A written answer to a case about a real company

shows.label: An analysis that ends in a recommendation
shows.means: Take a real dataset and a business question. Do the analysis, rank what to do with the expected return, state your assumptions, and defend it live.
artifacts: A deck or memo from a dataset: ranked recommendations, expected return, assumptions, a plan with milestones
A recorded walk-through answering hard questions on it

shows.label: Answer-first writing
shows.means: Lead with the answer. Put each supporting point under it.
artifacts: A one-page memo or short deck with one governing point

shows.label: A metric and a rhythm to run it by
shows.means: Pick the few numbers a team should watch and the meeting where they are read.
artifacts: A small dashboard and a one-page operating review for a real or student organisation

shows.label: A working tool built with AI
shows.means: Build a small internal tool on real or synthetic data, such as a customer-health view, and use it to do one piece of work.
artifacts: A demo of a self-built app or workflow
The work it produced, such as outreach drafted from the view

shows.label: An impact story with numbers
shows.means: Write up one piece of work: the problem, what you did, the number that moved.
artifacts: One project write-up with a measured result

data_scientist.label: Data Scientist
data_scientist.summary: Product data loops test SQL written live, a product-metrics case and experiment design. Take-homes are an analysis of a dataset with a written answer.

shows.label: SQL on real data
shows.means: Answer product questions with queries you write yourself.
artifacts: A set of queries on a public dataset, each with the question it answers

shows.label: A product-metrics case
shows.means: Define success for a product. Pick the metrics, say how each could mislead, and add guardrails.
artifacts: A metric framework for a product you use

shows.label: An experiment, designed and read
shows.means: Write the hypothesis, the unit, the metric, the sample size and the guardrails. Read a result and decide.
artifacts: An experiment design and a readout

shows.label: An analysis of a dataset, written up
shows.means: Take a dataset and a question. Do the analysis and write an answer a manager could act on.
artifacts: A notebook or report with the question, the method, the answer and its limits

shows.label: A metric drop, diagnosed
shows.means: Given a metric that fell, list the causes, check each against data, and say which it is.
artifacts: A short diagnosis write-up with the checks you ran

growth_manager.label: Growth Manager
growth_manager.summary: No company publishes a growth manager loop. Practitioners say the same thing: show applied growth work on real products.

shows.label: How a product grows
shows.means: Draw the loop that brings a real product its users. Name the weak step.
artifacts: A drawn growth loop with each step and what feeds the next
A write-up of one company's main growth engine

shows.label: An experiment, designed and read
shows.means: Write the hypothesis, the metric, the guardrails and the sample size. Then run it and say what you decided.
artifacts: An experiment write-up: hypothesis, metrics, design, result, decision

shows.label: A growth teardown, published
shows.means: Take a real product. Show its loop, a problem in it, and the experiment you would run.
artifacts: A public teardown; several make a portfolio

shows.label: Real channel work
shows.means: Run one paid ad on a social network and one on search. Audit a real site's SEO. Report what happened.
artifacts: An ad you ran with its numbers
An SEO health check of a real site

shows.label: A funnel, measured
shows.means: Set up tracking on a real funnel. Find where people drop and propose a fix.
artifacts: A funnel analysis with the query or dashboard behind it

pm.label: Product Manager
pm.summary: PM loops test product sense, analytical thinking and leadership. The newer programs and startup work trials ask for something shipped.

shows.label: Product sense
shows.means: Pick a user. Name their problem. Choose what to build and say what you cut.
artifacts: A written teardown of a real product
A redesign of one feature with the trade-offs stated

shows.label: Analytical thinking
shows.means: Say why the product exists. Define metrics someone could query. Pick one North Star metric, add guardrails, and set one team goal.
artifacts: A product rationale for a product you use
A metric framework with a North Star metric and guardrails
One team goal with the options you weighed
A trade-off decision with what would change your mind

shows.label: A plan for an open product problem
shows.means: Size the problem. Name who is affected. List solutions, put them in order, and say how you would measure success.
artifacts: A short deck: what you would build, in what order, and why
Ranked experiment ideas for a real product's new-user flow, three worked out

shows.label: Evidence from real users
shows.means: Talk to real users before you propose anything. Tie each idea to what they said.
artifacts: Notes from five user conversations with what changed in your plan

shows.label: Something shipped
shows.means: Build a small product, put it in front of users, and say what you learned from them.
artifacts: A working product with a 60-second demo
Short answers: the problem, what you built, your part, the result, what users taught you

shows.label: Leadership stories
shows.means: Write up your largest projects with context and results. Include a failure, a disagreement you resolved, and research that changed your plan.
artifacts: Three to five project write-ups with numbers

pmm.label: Product Marketing Manager
pmm.summary: PMM loops test positioning and a go-to-market case, often as a take-home deck presented to a panel, plus a small portfolio of written pieces.

shows.label: Positioning
shows.means: Say who the product is for, what they would use instead, what only it does, and why that matters to them.
artifacts: A positioning document for a real product
A sales pitch outline built from it

shows.label: A go-to-market or launch plan
shows.means: Plan a launch for a real product: the audience, the message, the channels, the measures.
artifacts: A launch plan as a deck or document you can present

shows.label: Launch writing
shows.means: Write the piece a launch needs: a blog post, a press release or a one-page data sheet.
artifacts: Two or three published pieces for real or imagined launches

shows.label: A marketing case with a point of view
shows.means: Take a brand or product problem. Structure it, weigh the options and commit to one recommendation.
artifacts: A written answer to a marketing case with a clear recommendation

shows.label: Material a seller can use
shows.means: Turn the positioning into something a salesperson would use on a call.
artifacts: A one-page battle card or pitch outline

product_designer.label: Product / UX Designer
product_designer.summary: Design loops rest on the portfolio: three to five case studies that show process, not only the final screens. Then a live design exercise and a critique of a shipped app.

shows.label: A case study that shows process
shows.means: State the user problem. Show the sketches, the directions you rejected, the final design, your part and the result.
artifacts: One case study in a consistent template; three to five make the portfolio

shows.label: A design exercise, worked end to end
shows.means: From a one-line prompt: the goal, the audience, their needs, ranked ideas, a sketched solution, how you would measure it.
artifacts: A written-up design exercise with sketches of several directions

shows.label: A critique of a shipped app
shows.means: Pick an app you use. Say what works, what does not, and why the team likely chose it.
artifacts: A written or recorded critique of one app

shows.label: One interaction, designed for a real product
shows.means: Design one named interaction in a real product, in its own design language.
artifacts: A prototype of the interaction with the states and edge cases

shows.label: Research that feeds a decision
shows.means: Write the questions, talk to a few users, and say what the findings change.
artifacts: A research plan, an interview guide and a one-page findings summary

software_engineer.label: Software Engineer
software_engineer.summary: Big Tech still tests algorithms and system design, now with an AI assistant in the room. Startups hire on real work: a bug fixed in an unfamiliar codebase, an API integrated from its docs, a trial project.

shows.label: Coding fundamentals
shows.means: Solve problems with the core data structures and algorithms. Explain your approach and its cost as you go.
artifacts: A tracked set of solved problems with notes on the pattern each uses

shows.label: Work in a codebase you did not write
shows.means: Find and fix a real bug in an open-source project. Explain how you found it.
artifacts: A merged or open pull request with the reasoning written up

shows.label: Build against an API from its docs
shows.means: Read the documentation of a real API and ship something small that uses it.
artifacts: A working integration with a short README

shows.label: System design
shows.means: State the requirements. Estimate the load. Draw the parts and say what you traded away.
artifacts: A design write-up with a diagram, estimates and trade-offs for a system you built or use

shows.label: Work with an AI assistant and judge its output
shows.means: Build with an AI tool. Review what it wrote, find what is wrong, and say why.
artifacts: A project log showing where you corrected or rejected the assistant's code

shows.label: A shipped project with other people
shows.means: Ship a small feature that real users touch, ideally with at least one other person.
artifacts: A deployed project, its repository, and a note on who did what

shows.label: Stories with results
shows.means: Write up past work with numbers. Include a failure and what you learned.
artifacts: A bank of stories in situation, action, result form
